title: The review/leaderboard release and scoring pipeline has unresolved terminal-state and time semantics

original_titles.title: Missing terminal transitions: stage RELEASED->FINAL and submission DISPUTED->RESOLVED
Leaderboard snapshots event-driven only; no interval snapshot job; responses not cacheable

problem: The audit claims missing RELEASED->FINAL and DISPUTED->RESOLVED transitions, event-driven-only leaderboard snapshots and app-server-clock cutoffs. Some state machines have been revised for the four-level flow, so the exact terminal-state semantics need an up-to-date state diagram and tests.
impact: Ambiguous terminal transitions can leave submissions/disputes in non-terminal states or results with inconsistent ranking/cutoff behavior.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Publish one canonical event/stage/submission/dispute state diagram, including terminal and post-release states.
Compare every transition in the backend and DB constraints against the diagram; remove impossible transitions and add missing authorized transitions.
Use database time for leaderboard cutoff/release and a deterministic snapshot version sequence.
Add transition-table tests for every valid/invalid edge and post-release dispute/correction behavior.

acceptance_criteria: Every state machine has a defined terminal state and transition owner.
Leaderboard ordering/cutoff is deterministic and based on DB time.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
